_comment: Example credo LAN peer relay config. Copy to ~/.claude/credo/peer-lan.json (or point CREDO_PEER_LAN_CONFIG at it) and edit. The relay is a no-op until this file exists; once it does, it starts automatically on session start (one daemon per machine) and can be disabled with CREDO_PEER_LAN set to 0/false/no/off.
_token_comment: The shared token is OPTIONAL. Left empty (as below) or omitted entirely, the relay runs TOKEN-LESS - the casual default for a trusted home LAN. WITHOUT a token, any device that can reach listen_host:listen_port can send messages to your sessions (gated only by the receiving session's own consent prompt; the relay never forges a trusted sender). Set the SAME non-empty token on every machine to restrict messaging to your own devices - recommended on untrusted or company networks. A machine whose token differs from a token-requiring peer is rejected by that peer. Enabling it later is just adding the same token here on every machine - no code change.
_peers_comment: IMPORTANT: each peers[].name MUST equal that remote machine's own this_machine value. A remote session only materializes (its holder + descriptor are created) when the sender machine's this_machine matches a configured peer name here. A mismatch means the remote peer silently never appears. Example: on pc-hub below, the laptop machine must set this_machine to 'laptop' and the workbench machine must set this_machine to 'workbench'.
